name: pranaviln
text:
Hey X 👋

If we haven't met, I'm pranavi (pronounced pren-uh-vee).

I'm building Mixr, an iOS DJ app, with Cursor and documenting everything I learn in my Designing by Building 🎧 series.

If you're into music, mixing, or building software, I'd love to connect!

#buildinpublic #DesignEngineering

name: pranaviln
text:
I'm a product designer who knows how to code.

Somewhere along the way, I realized I was making better design decisions in SwiftUI than I ever was in Figma.

So I'm starting an experiement.

Instead of treating code as the final step of design, I'm making it the design process.

I'm building an app from scratch and documenting every design decision along the way.

I'm calling it Designing by Building. 🎧

name: pranaviln
text:
I want to learn how to DJ, but the problem is...

I don't know music theory. 
I can't play an instrument. 
And I've never mixed a song before.

But I do know how to code.

So instead of buying a DJ set, I started building an app.

I've landed on Mixr, an iOS DJ app that makes remixing songs easy for beginners.

More accessible? Definitely. Less expensive? Let's see how many Cursor credits I use and find out. 

This is Designing by Building. 🎧

name: pranaviln
text:
Day 1 🎧 Designing by Building 

I stopped spending weeks perfecting Figma files and instead started designing directly in SwiftUI.

Every component starts as running code, not a mockup.

This was the first thing I built: a design system to validate every color, typography style, glass material, button, and waveform before touching the actual app.

It's not glamorous, but it's the foundation for everything that'll come after.

Over the next few weeks I'll be sharing how Mixr will evolve from this screen into a real iPhone app.

name: pranaviln
text:
Bet you couldn't tell each effects card has a different glow value.

Reverb and Echo have stronger glows because they're darker.

Auto has the strongest glow because I want people to click it.

Same number values ≠ same visual weight.🤯

name: pranaviln
text:
Day 4 🎧 Designing by Building

Spent the last two days designing these effects cards, but it was worth it cause they're my favorite part of the app😭

I was at HBO Max during the HBO -> HBO Max redesign. A design trick I learned:

Never make glass perfectly uniform.

✨ Slightly different highlights.
✨ Different bubble locations each card.
✨ Glow that reflects onto neighboring cards.

Tiny imperfections make the glass feel more dynamic and alive.

name: pranaviln
text:
Day 5 🎧 Designing by Building

Hooked up song importing today 🎉

The rest updated itself: song chips, waveforms, metadata values.

My favorite Cursor moment because it connected related UI without me asking. It understood how my app should behave. 

That's when the app started feeling like a product and not a collection of screens.

#buildinpublic

name: pranaviln
text:
Designing by Building 🎧 Design Decision:

I had 2 options for the Auto effects card: Pearl White and Rainbow Iridescent

✨White = the absence of color.

🌈Rainbow = all the colors.

Since Auto combines multiple effects, rainbow iridescent felt more intuitive (and prettier).

#buildinpublic #DesignEngineering

name: pranaviln
text:
Day 7 🎧 Designing by Building

Added:

✂️ Split
📄 Duplicate
🗑️ Delete
🤏 Drag & drop

The hard part was deciding how they should behave. Drag & drop behavior was the hardest design decision I had to make.

When a clip is dropped in the middle of others, do the neighbors shift left or right? At what threshold is the direction decided?

After two days, it clicked.

Drop it in the middle of a clip → split clip → sandwich between old one🤯

Could I have figured this out in five minutes by looking at other apps?

Absolutely.

That's why we do competitive analysis, folks.

name: pranaviln
text:
🎶 "More than a Feeling"

Cursor helps me move fast, but real design work still happens in a loop:  

build → run → feel → adjust  

tbh "feel coding" makes more sense than "vibe coding." what even are vibes? petition to have it changed!

name: pranaviln
text:
Designing by Building 🎧 Tip: Get closer to the material.  

Apple's glass materials behave differently when they're real. I didn't fully understand until I built with SwiftUI. Motion and interaction exposed design flaws earlier than mockups.  

What's something you only noticed when you started building your designs?

name: pranaviln
text:
Designing by Building 🎧 Me vs. AI:

For my segmented control, I only show "beats" on the selected option.

Adding "beats" to every option felt cluttered. Removing it entirely made the UI confusing.

It's a tradeoff between clarity and simplicity: AI would choose one extreme or the other. Only I could find this compromise.

PS: Thank you to everyone who suggested using beats instead of seconds for transitions! ❤️

name: pranaviln
text:
Day 10 🎧 Designing by Building

Not a lot of code today, but a lot of research for my "Auto" feature!

I was trying to answer the questions:
• What makes a good remix?
• How many times should a song alternate in a mashup?
• How should the strategy change for 1 song vs. 2 vs. 5, and how can we generalize these rules?

If anyone has suggestions on what they like to hear, let me know!

name: pranaviln
text:
10 Things I've learned building Mixr:

1. Building is the fastest way to improve taste.
2. Good prompts start with good references.
3. Design systems teach AI how the product looks. Take time to establish one.
4. The quality of AI output is limited by the quality of your product thinking.
5. Beginners need interfaces designed for their vocabulary, not yours.
7. Visual alignment matters more than mathematical alignment.
8. The smallest UI details are often the most memorable.
9. The "obvious" interaction isn't obvious until you've explored five bad ones.
6. If you can't explain it in a prompt, you haven't researched it enough.
10. The best design decisions happen after the app runs.

Start coding (it's easy with Cursor, Codex, Claude)!
